summary: Iteration 10 focused frontend test on the new Home bento (asymmetric masonry). Grid contract mostly holds: dense CSS-Grid packing, object-fit:contain, 16-px inner padding, 12 tiles rendered, admin home_order sequence respected via useGallery. However, the requirement of at least 3 distinct grid-column span values is NOT met at desktop 1920 — only 'span 4' and 'span 6' appear in practice because all landscape source images share ratio ~1.5 (falls in the 6-span bucket) and all portraits fall in the 4-span bucket. Regressions (Consult modal validation, 'Other Services' dropdown, WhatsApp placement, footer) all pass.

ui_bugs.issue: At desktop 1920×1080, only 2 unique grid-column span values are emitted ('span 4' and 'span 6') across all 12 tiles. Spec requires >=3 distinct spans (e.g., 3, 4, 5, 6, 7). Root cause: real project images all share ratio ~1.5 (→ 6-span bucket) and portraits share ratio ~0.7-0.78 (→ 4-span bucket); no image ever satisfies the >=1.55 (span 7), 1.05-1.25 (span 5), or <0.65 (span 3) branches. Suggestion: mix in the deterministic fallback pattern [6,4,5,3,4,6,3,5,4,6,4,3] as a secondary variation source (e.g., blend index-based nudge for ratios sitting on bucket boundaries), or widen the range bands, or explicitly override 3-4 tiles to span 3/5/7 by index to guarantee visual rhythm.

issues: Because only 2 span sizes appear, wide (span 6) tiles pair well but the layout reads slightly more repetitive than the editorial brief intends. Not blocky-square (heights vary 484-708 px), but variety could be richer.

verification_evidence.consult_modal: opens, validation shows 'Please enter your name', 'Other Services' present in Service Type dropdown along with Interiors and Restoration & Renovation
verification_evidence.whatsapp_icons_home: footer-whatsapp (in footer) + consultation-whatsapp (inside modal only). No WhatsApp icon next to on-page ConsultButtons.
verification_evidence.admin_sequence_logic: HomeGallery.jsx sorts featured photos by home_order asc (nulls last) then created_at — matches spec

action_items: Increase span diversity so >=3 distinct grid-column values render in real data. Options: (a) intercalate the fallback deterministic pattern based on tile index for a portion of tiles, (b) widen buckets so 1600×1067 (ratio 1.5) sometimes maps to span 5 or span 7 by rotating on index, (c) explicitly override tiles at indexes [0, 4, 8] to span 3/5/7 for editorial rhythm.
critical_code_review_comments: colSpanFor is purely ratio-driven and ignores the index fallback pattern once ratio is known — this creates the 2-span-only pathology when source data has homogeneous ratios. Consider a hybrid: `if(index in [0,4,8,11]) return fallback[index]` then ratio-based for the rest.

grid-row-span calculation uses gap value that differs from CSS at each breakpoint — currently hard-coded {12,16,20}. This works but should ideally derive from CSS custom properties to stay DRY if gaps ever change.
PLACEHOLDERS array uses 10 Pexels URLs but the useMemo cap is 12; if realProjects + featured yield <2 items, mobile users see mostly stock photography. Consider bumping to 12 placeholders.
seed_data_creation: None — public gallery already returns enough photos to fill 12 tiles.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The bento is at [data-testid=home-gallery-section] with tiles [data-testid=home-bento-tile-{0..11}]. Use section.scroll_into_view_if_needed() — Lenis intercepts window.scrollTo. To verify the >=3 span fix, evaluate `[...new Set(Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid^=home-bento-tile-]')).map(t=>getComputedStyle(t).gridColumn))]` at 1920×1080 after tiles finish loading (2-3s wait after scroll). Mobile is 4-col layout with spans 2 and 4 (acceptable for 4-col viewport).
